pairs.subject: app-shell
pairs.evidence: src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx:119 The application shell renders a placeholder skeleton across the persistent top bar and navigation rail during Zustand store hydration rather than painting immediately from local knowledge.

techniques.evidence: src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx:119 The shell frame renders a placeholder skeleton over the navigation rail and top bar during store hydration, and ModuleSkeleton lacks a warm-path appearance delay.
src/components/layout/SidebarL2/StatusBadge.tsx:19 Task status is indicated by color alone on a rounded dot with no alert icon or shape, and failed states have no exposure-based clearing rule.
src/components/layout/SidebarL1.tsx:19 Expand and collapse rail posture is persisted in the store, icons and active indicators survive collapse, and flyout reveals appear on hover and keyboard focus.
src/components/layout/SidebarL2/index.tsx:92 Navigation interactions directly call separate sub-module and category setters rather than passing through the unified navigateToModule entry point.

declined.subject: app-shell
declined.reason: withdrawn after review: reviewer (sonnet): The claim that the direct setters bypass history synchronization is contradicted by src/hooks/useShellRouteSync.ts, which subscribes to useNavigationStore and pushes a history entry on any change to the visible module, whichever setter caused it. The useSuspend.ts claim that the shell lacks a restor
